subject: Discovery recap: success metrics, evaluation modes, and next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Calvin Brooks <calvin@westbridgehealth.com>, Priya Suresh <priya@westbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap and proposed success criteria / eval modes

Calvin / Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed path for the trial so we can align on scope and ownership. I wanted to get these into writing so we can move quickly.

Top-level: goal is to validate Redwood inference on two primary use cases: (1) discharge-summary extraction (high precision required) and (2) triage suggestion prompts (latency-sensitive). You asked for both an objective offline evaluation and a short online observation (shadow) to validate production behavior.

Proposed success criteria (attached as Westbridge_Success_Criteria.xlsx):
- Discharge extraction: precision >= 92% (primary), recall >= 85% (secondary)
- Triage suggestions: mean 95th-percentile latency <= 300ms
- Hallucination rate (factual errors per 1k tokens) <= 1.5
- Clinician accept rate (manual QA spot checks) >= 88%
- No PII leakage in returned payloads (must pass privacy scan)

Evaluation modes (choose both or one):
1) Offline batch eval — we run curated test sets & your anonymized historical records through the model, score against golden labels. Pros: fastest to iterate, deterministic. Cons: may not catch streaming/latency artifacts.
2) Online shadow (live) — route real traffic to Redwood in shadow mode with a human-in-loop review for a subset. Pros: catches production regressions, latency, and interaction effects. Cons: requires production access and a short observation window (we recommend 7–14 days) and clear rollback triggers.

Initial timeline (proposed):
- Week 0–1: NDA (if outstanding), finalize success criteria, pick eval mode(s) and dataset slices
- Week 2: Data handoff and ingestion (secure S3 transfer; we support SFTP/Glue connectors)
- Week 3: Offline eval run + report (if chosen)
- Week 4–6: Online shadowing (if chosen) + clinician QA + final acceptance

Owners:
- Redwood AE / owner: Naomi Feldman (me) — commercial questions, milestones, stakeholder coordination
- Redwood Ops: Stephanie Nguyen — contract/DocuSign & trial onboarding logistics
- Redwood Solutions / Tech lead: Marcus Lin — infra, data connectors, eval rubric execution
- Westbridge: Calvin Brooks (trial sponsor) + Priya Suresh (clinical QA owner)

Attachments: Westbridge_Success_Criteria.xlsx, Redwood_Trial_Scope.docx. I also uploaded the HubSpot deal link and a draft DocuSign for the trial SLA to the Drive folder (links below). Please confirm the success criteria and whether you prefer "offline-first" or "shadow-first" (or both). Once you confirm we’ll lock timeline and get Stephanie to send a DocuSign for the trial scope.

Thanks — look forward to your thoughts.

—
Naomi Feldman

Thanks Naomi — useful summary. A few questions before we finalize:

1) Weighting: do you expect us to treat precision as a hard gate for discharge extraction (i.e., must meet 92%) or is this part of a weighted score with clinician accept rate?
2) For the online shadow, what percentage of production requests would be shadowed and how do you handle mismatches between downstream systems when the model is in shadow?
3) Data privacy: we will only allow PHI to leave our VPC for production in a private deployment. Can offline runs be done on pseudonymized extracts in Redwood hosted infra?
4) Can you share a short rubric for how you score hallucinations vs acceptable paraphrase?

Also, I see the DocuSign link in your drive but wanted to confirm: we signed and returned the standard NDA yesterday (attached NDA_signed.pdf). Can you confirm you received it?

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Calvin Brooks <calvin@westbridgehealth.com>, Priya Suresh <priya@westbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap and proposed success criteria / eval modes

Calvin — great questions, answered inline below. I also attached a one-page rubric summary to the Drive folder for quick review.

1) Weighting: recommend a two-tier approach: precision for discharge extraction as a hard gate (pass/fail) at >=92% for acceptance. Clinician accept rate is a secondary quality gate (weighted 30%). Overall acceptance requires the hard gate plus combined score >= 85%. We can tweak thresholds with you — want to keep the hard gate for patient-safety use cases.

2) Shadow sampling: we typically start with 10–15% of eligible production requests in shadow mode and route full traffic to your system as normal. Redwood records the model outputs in a sandbox; we create a reconciliation layer that maps our outputs to your downstream keys so you can compare side-by-side. If downstream schema mismatches occur, we fall back to a small adapter script (we’ll coordinate with Marcus).

3) Data privacy: yes — offline runs can be done on pseudonymized extracts in our hosted environment, or we can run them inside your private deployment (Redwood Private) if you prefer. For PHI-sensitive workloads we recommend private deployment for the shadow phase.

4) Hallucination rubric (high-level):
- Factual error (0.0–1.0): 1.0 = incorrect factual claim affecting clinical decision; 0.5 = minor factual drift; 0.0 = factually correct or paraphrase
- Paraphrase tolerance: acceptable if clinical meaning unchanged
- Severity weighting: errors that change triage/diagnosis are multiplied by 2

Also: NDA received, thanks — I see the signed copy in the folder (NDA_signed.pdf).

Next steps I propose: please confirm (A) you accept the hard gate + weighted acceptance approach, (B) whether you want us to run an offline pass first or go straight to a short shadow, and (C) who from Clinical QA will be the point people. Once we have that I’ll ask Stephanie to issue the DocuSign trial scope and schedule the data-handoff window.

—
Naomi

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap and proposed success criteria / eval modes

Calvin / Priya / team — quick technical confirmation and proposed rubric details from the solutions side. High level: both modes are feasible; tradeoffs and minimal steps below.

Feasibility notes:
- Offline batch: we need a 2–4k example golden-label slice (CSV/JSONL) with canonical keys for matching. We can run a full sweep in ~36–48 hours depending on sequence lengths.
- Shadow: requires a small adapter that maps Westbridge request IDs to our shadow records; we can provide a lightweight Lambda adapter or a docker sidecar. VPN or private peering is optional if you prefer to post to a secured S3 endpoint.

Proposed grading rubric (numeric, automated where possible):
- Precision (discharge extraction): 50 points (automated label compare)
- Recall (discharge extraction): 20 points
- Latency (triage): 10 points (penalty kicks for 95th percentile > threshold)
- Hallucination / factual correctness: 15 points (manual sampling + automated factual checks)
- Clinician accept rate: 5 points (human spot-checks)

Pass threshold: >= 85/100 AND precision gate >= 92%. If any single safety-critical hallucination is found in the sample that changes clinical intent, trial fails and we must root-cause before re-run.

Operational checklist for shadowing:
- Provide 3 days of replay traffic prior to turning on 10% shadowing for warm-up
- Instrumentation: token-level latency logs, model version id, request hash (no PHI in logs)
- Automated privacy scan on outputs (we have a scanner that flags PII)
- Sampling plan: random 10% + targeted 100% for discharge-summary type messages for the first 48 hours

Estimated Redwood resource commitment & cost note:
- Small trial (2–4 weeks, 10–15% shadow): we reserve 1 GPU shard for the shadow and 1 small CPU host for batching; approximate incremental cost $2,800/week (est; for planning only). We can convert to a PoC credit arrangement if helpful.

I’ll prepare a short tech-runbook and the automated rubric script; Naomi / Stephanie — let me know if you want me to include a quick demo run with synthetic data this week.

—
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
